subject: Private deployment: pinning policy, maintenance window & rollback acceptance
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jae Park <jae.park@acmehealth.com>, Acme Health CloudOps <ops@acmehealth.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Oct 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment: pinning policy, maintenance window & rollback acceptance

Hi team —

Following yesterday's sync with Acme Health, they want final alignment on how we manage version pinning and the rollback guarantees for their private VPC deployment ahead of the Nov 3 maintenance window. They are sensitive to any model/runtime change during the fiscal quarter close, and asked for written acceptance criteria.

I put a first-pass checklist and proposed pinning policy in the attached acme_preflight_checklist.xlsx and a short playbook in rollback_playbook_v2.md. Key asks from Acme:
- 72-hour advance notice for any pin/unpin operation that affects customer-visible behavior
- Clear abort criteria and SLIs for automatic abort
- Rehearsed rollback steps and an owner for each step

Questions for us:
1) Can we commit to a two-week pin for minor runtime patches (non-model changes) with the automatic rollback window if token error rate > 0.6%?
2) For major model version upgrades (e.g., 2.x -> 3.x), recommend staged pinning: 1-week canary, 2-week staged, then 4-week stable. Would leadership OK this cadence?
3) Who is the on-call/exec for an emergency unpin if we're forced to abort?

Would appreciate rapid feedback — Acme expects a signed plan by EOD Wed so they can route procurement.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment stubs: acme_preflight_checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet), rollback_playbook_v2.md (markdown), pinning-policy-summary.pdf (one-pager)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jae Park <jae.park@acmehealth.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Oct 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: pinning policy, maintenance window & rollback acceptance

Marissa / all —

Short answers up front:
- Two-week pin for minor runtime patches: yes, operationally feasible if we classify patches as "non-invasive" (no KV schema or network changes). We'll need feature flags and an automated health gate.
- Automatic rollback threshold: 0.6% token error rate is reasonable as a conservative gate, but we should tie it to both token error and 5-minute p99 latency spike to avoid false positives. Recommend combined condition: (token_error_rate > 0.6% for 5m) OR (p99 latency > 2x baseline for 10m).
- Major model upgrades: staged cadence below sounds good, but extend the canary to 2 weeks for Acme since they are high-risk and stateful (long-running KV usage).

Operational notes:
- Rollback steps are in rollback_playbook_v2.md — primary will be Soojin for orchestrating network-level pin (rollback to pinned image + cache invalidation), Laura for customer comms, Karthik for automation. We should add a preflight smoke test that verifies KV hitrate and streaming latencies on a 10-minute window before committing.

I'll add the combined gate to the playbook and upload a revised checklist within the hour. Markus — recommend we approve this pattern as a one-off for Acme and then generalize into the team playbook.

- Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Private Deployments, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Attachment references: will update acme_preflight_checklist.xlsx -> tab "gates"

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jae Park <jae.park@acmehealth.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Oct 2028 13:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: pinning policy, maintenance window & rollback acceptance

Thanks — good first pass. A few leadership-level decisions so we can give Acme a clear yes/no: 

1) Pin duration: Approve two-week pin for minor runtime patches. Document must specify a hard auto-unpin timeout and manual override path for legal/compliance requests.

2) Gates & metrics: Approve combined gate (token error OR p99 latency) as the abort condition. Add a secondary human-ack gate for any abort inside Acme's business hours (08:00-18:00 local).

3) Major upgrades: Approve staged approach but set canary to 2 weeks for Acme. For general customers, keep 1-week canary but require a runbook test pass.

4) Emergency unpin owner: Assign Soojin as primary for rollout orchestration and Karthik as fallback. Laura to lead external comms if we trigger rollback.

Please update rollback_playbook_v2.md with these decisions and the clear owner matrix by EOD tomorrow. Marissa — copy these items into a single-line acceptance letter for Acme (they want a succinct statement they can attach to procurement).

-Markus
Markus Klein
VP, Customer Success (Acting)
markus_klein@redwood.ai

P.S. We should add a notes field in our ticket so Finance can track credits if we hit a rollback-triggered SLA. I'll loop in finance if necessary.

From: Jae Park <jae.park@acmehealth.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Acme Health CloudOps <ops@acmehealth.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Oct 2028 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment: pinning policy, maintenance window & rollback acceptance

Markus / team —

Thanks for the clear answers and the owner matrix. Acme accepts the two-week pin for minor runtime patches with the combined gate and the 2-week canary for major upgrades. We also confirm the maintenance window of Nov 3-4 as our preferred quiet window; our procurement team requested the one-line acceptance for their file.

I attached a short acceptance note that we will sign and return once your legal team attaches the standard MSA addendum. If you can send the one-line acceptance text (as Marissa suggested) today, I will push the DocuSign flow on our side.

Appreciate everyone's responsiveness.

—Jae Park
Director, Cloud Operations
Acme Health
ops@acmehealth.com

Attachment stubs: acme-signed-acceptance-placeholder.txt (will be replaced by DocuSign)
